label: late copy-phase input p (fed-back p near end of long sequences)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is p (the model just output p and it is fed back): 100% of activations have in_tok == p. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases or on any other input token. It is concentrated late in long sequences: 93% of mass is at L = 9, and the rate rises sharply with t (t = 16-17 holds about 70% of mass). It is stronger when the next output is y or p (as in p p y or p y), and to a lesser degree 2, k, g, r. Top activations (up to 1.4) are p at recall_idx 7 in L = 9 sequences ending in ...p p y or ...p y. Precision is very low: the feature is active on only about 1.5% of late copy-phase p inputs, and false positives look the same at the token level (e.g. ...s p y g with p at step 16 stays inactive). So whatever additionally gates it is not captured by token or position variables. The predicate copy-phase in_tok == p and t >= 13 captures about 95% of activations and 96% of mass. Adding out_tok in {y, p} and t >= 16 raises dev F1 only to 0.33.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: p, -, h, x, o, q; least: g, i, m, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: y, p, 2, k, g, r; least: l, w, u, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
